HistoricalPeriod: Third Intermediate Period, 22nd Dynasty, c. 925 BC
ArtifactDate: 11th–8th centuries BC (royal city; tombs c. 1000–900 BC)
CurrentLocation: In situ, Nile Delta, Egypt; finds in the Egyptian Museum, Cairo
Description: The Delta capital whose royal necropolis Pierre Montet uncovered intact, including the silver coffin of Psusennes I and the gold mask of Shoshenq II. Tanis is the biblical Zoan, the city named when Hebron's antiquity is measured and where the psalmist says God worked wonders in Egypt.
BiblicalSignificance: Zoan is where Egypt's power was displayed and where, the psalm says, God displayed His. A royal tomb untouched by robbers, full of silver and gold, is a small parable of the Exodus itself: Egypt's wealth could not buy what Israel's God gave freely.
Interpretations: Scholars agree Tanis is biblical Zoan; the royal tombs are securely dated, and their value for the Bible is the Egyptian royal world of the Divided Monarchy period.
